title: Webhook proxy to map OpenAI-style tools to legacy function contracts
creator: Sofia Kim
description: Build a lightweight webhook/proxy adapter in the runtime that accepts OpenAI-style tool invocation payloads (tool name + JSON args + streaming chunk semantics) and translates them into our legacy function invocation schema used by private deployments and older SDKs. This adapter enables customers that supply OpenAI-style tool manifests to continue operating without changing existing legacy backends, while preserving streaming and structured-output guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter correctly maps tool names and aliases to legacy function ids (configurable alias registry).
Parameter shapes are transformed according to mapping rules (snake_case<->camelCase), with type coercion and validation errors returned with structured diagnostic payloads.
Streaming responses from legacy functions are re-encoded to OpenAI-style streaming chunks with ordering and partial-parse safety guarantees.
End-to-end tests (unit + integration) that validate name collisions, missing params, and backpressure scenarios pass in CI.
Canary rollout telemetry shows no regression in 99th percentile end-to-end latency for instrumented customers.
Fallback policy: on adapter failure, requests follow configured fallback (reject, route to fallback model, or return standardized error).
implementation_notes: Create adapter as a separate module in runtime/compat with a minimal public surface: /v1/tool-proxy/invoke
Design alias registry as a small key-value store backed by existing config service; support hot-reload for mapping updates.
Streaming: use existing runtime chunking layer but add an explicit provenance header (x-rw-provenance) to each chunk to record original toolName and legacyFnId.
Parameter marshalling: implement schema-driven mappers using existing model schemas when available, otherwise fall back to permissive JSON passthrough with validation warnings.
Telemetry: emit mapping events and per-request histogram for transformation latency and error-codes; tag events with customer_id and route_id.
Safety: validate that functions that mutate customer data require explicit allowlist and SSO-scoped tokens; otherwise reject with 403.
Testing: include recorded fixture harness to simulate streamed partial frames and reassembly edge cases.
Docs: add migration guide and example manifests in Console docs and a short RFC in Confluence (link below).
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose a proxy approach vs. changing legacy backends to avoid high-risk migration for customers (decision by infra + product).
2026-03-03: Agreed on alias registry model (config store + hot-reload) instead of embedding mappings in code to support ops-driven fixes.
2026-03-05: Chose to preserve streaming chunk boundaries from legacy functions where possible and wrap partial frames with provenance metadata rather than re-chunking aggressively.
2026-03-08: Security sign-off required for function invocations that touch PII; added allowlist and token-scope validation step.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created by Sofia Kim; initial scoping and estimate; assigned to Matt Reynolds.
2026-03-03: Prototype of name-alias matcher implemented (ENG-branch: feature/compat/proxy-alias); unit tests for simple name collisions added.
2026-03-05: Streaming chunk header added to prototype; discovered ordering bug when legacy function emits duplicate final frames — created test fixture to reproduce (see PR).
2026-03-07: Design review with PM (Diego Alvarez) and Security (Aisha Patel). Security requested explicit allowlist and audit events for each mapped invocation.
2026-03-09: Integration test matrix added for camelCase<->snake_case param permutations and missing-parameter behaviors.
2026-03-10: Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421 — seeking review from runtime-maintainers and telemetry team.
2026-03-10: Canary rollout plan drafted; will target 5% of traffic for two business days and monitor mapping error rate and tail latency.

review_feedback: Aisha (Security): require token-scope verification and audit events; reject invocations to disallowed legacy functions.
Diego (PM): ensure alias registry supports time-bounded aliases to make temporary mappings easy during migrations.
Elena (Telemetry): include mapping_id and transformation_latency in emitted events; prefer exponential histogram for latency buckets.
Luke (Runtime): prefer reusing existing chunking layer rather than introducing new streaming infra to reduce risk.
open_tasks: Complete PR addressing ordering bug in streaming reassembly (assigned to Matt).
Add canary gating in the operator control plane and a feature flag for per-customer enablement.
Implement allowlist UI in Console (coord with PM/Design).
Run privacy review for customers in EU and APAC regions.
